anchors.heading: Christopher Columbus

image.attribution: Ridolfo del Ghirlandaio — Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.caption: Christopher Columbus
image.commons_file: File:Ridolfo del Ghirlandaio - Ritratto di Cristoforo Colombo (1520).jpg

anchors.prose: Christopher Columbus, a Genoese navigator, persuaded Ferdinand and Isabella at Córdoba in January to sponsor a westward voyage to the East Indies. The Capitulations of Santa Fe, signed in April, granted him titles and a share of riches. A royal decree in April forced the port of Palos to supply two ships; with the Pinzón brothers, he sailed on 3 August with the Niña, Pinta, and Santa María. After a stop at La Gomera on 6 September, the expedition crossed the Atlantic. On 7 October, with mutiny threatening after 29 days without land, flocks of birds prompted a course change. Land was sighted at dawn on 12 October by Rodrigo de Triana; Columbus went ashore on Guanahani, which he renamed San Salvador, and called the natives indios. He reached Cuba on 28 October and Hispaniola on 5 December.

quote.text: He developed a plan to seek a western sea passage to the East Indies, hoping to profit from the lucrative spice trade. After the Granada War, and Columbus's persistent lobbying in multiple kingdoms, the Catholic Monarchs, Queen Isabella I and King Ferdinand II, agreed to sponsor a journey west.

records: Believing he has reached the East Indies, Christopher Columbus and his expedition of three ships make landfall in the Caribbean and land on the island of Guanahani, now part of the Bahamas. He names the island "San Salvador". Earlier in the day, sailor Rodrigo de Triana on the Pinta had become the first person to spot land. Because of his belief that he is in the East Indies, Columbus refers to the natives as "indios".

Christopher Columbus meets Ferdinand and Isabella at the Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos in Córdoba, Andalusia, and persuades them to support his Atlantic voyage intended to find a new route to the East Indies.
The Capitulations of Santa Fe are signed between Christopher Columbus and the Crown of Castile, agreeing on arrangements for his forthcoming voyage.

At the shipbuilding town of Palos de la Frontera in Spain, an April 30 decree of Queen Isabella of Castile and King Ferdinand of Aragon is read aloud to the residents, directing that two ships are to be delivered to Christopher Columbus and people chosen by the Pinzon brothers will be required to travel on the voyage westward "by command of Their Highnesses").

The Genoese navigator Christopher Columbus sails with three ships (Niña, Pinta and Santa María) from Palos de la Frontera, in the service of the Crown of Castile, on his first voyage across the Atlantic Ocean, intending to reach Asia.
Christopher Columbus sails from La Gomera in the Canary Islands, his final port of call before crossing the Atlantic Ocean for the first time.

The Columbus expedition, having seen no land for 29 days while sailing eastward, and with some of its sailors threatening to mutiny, spots large flocks of birds, confirming that land is ahead. Christopher Columbus orders a change of course to follow the flight direction of the birds.
Christopher Columbus lands in what is now the Holguín Province of the island of Cuba.
Christopher Columbus becomes the first European to set foot on the island of Hispaniola in present day northwestern Haiti.

anchors.prose: Cardinal Rodrigo Borja was elected pope unanimously on the fourth ballot of the conclave that opened on 8 August in the Sistine Chapel. The first ballot had split the 23 cardinals among Oliviero Carafa (9 votes), Borja (7), and Giuliano della Rovere (5), with two blank. Borja took the name Alexander VI on 11 August, becoming the 214th pope.

quote.text: Pope Alexander VI (Italian: Alessandro VI, Valencian: Alexandre VI, Spanish: Alejandro VI; born Roderic de Borja y Llançol  epithet: Valentinus ("The Valencian"); c. 1431 – 18 August 1503) was head of the Catholic Church and leader of the Papal States from 11 August 1492 until his death in 1503.

records: Cardinal Rodrigo Borja is unanimously elected on the fourth ballot of the papal conclave, and takes the name of Pope Alexander VI, 214th pope of the Roman Catholic Church.
11 August: Spanish cardinal Rodrigo de Borja is elected Pope Alexander VI

The papal conclave, the first to be held in the Sistine Chapel, begins balloting with 23 of the 27 members of the College of Cardinals in attendance. With 16 votes needed for the required two-thirds majority, the first ballot is split among three candidates, with Oliviero Carafa receiving 9, Rodrigo Borja 7 and Giuliano della Rovere 5, while two cast a blank vote.

anchors.prose: On 2 January, Muhammad XI of Granada surrendered the city and the Alhambra to Ferdinand and Isabella after a long siege, ending the Granada War and the centuries-long Reconquista. The fall brought 780 years of Muslim rule in Al-Andalus to a close.

quote.text: The Granada War was a series of military campaigns between 1482 and 1492 during the reign of the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon, against the Nasrid dynasty's Emirate of Granada. It ended with the defeat of Granada and its annexation by Castile, ending the last remnant of Islamic rule on the Iberian peninsula.

records: End Of The Reconquista

Fall of Granada: Muhammad XI, the last Emir of Granada, surrenders his city to the army of the Catholic Monarchs (Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile) after a lengthy siege, ending the ten-year Granada War and the centuries-long Reconquista, and bringing an end to 780 years of Muslim control in Al-Andalus.

anchors.prose: Henry VII of England dispatched an expedition that laid siege to Boulogne on 3 October. On 3 November, the Peace of Étaples was agreed with Charles VIII of France: the French paid £153,000 for Henry to withdraw, and ended support for the pretender Perkin Warbeck.

quote.text: The Peace of Étaples was signed on 3 November 1492 in Étaples between Charles VIII of France and Henry VII of England. Charles agreed to end his support for the Yorkist Pretender Perkin Warbeck, in return for being recognised as ruler of the Duchy of Brittany.

records: Henry VII dispatches an English expedition to lay Siege of Boulogne

anchors.prose: Pope Innocent VIII died on 25 July at age 59 from catarrh. In May, he had met with Ottoman envoys at Santa Maria del Popolo, who presented the Holy Lance and offered 120,000 crowns of gold plus an annual subsidy for the continued imprisonment of Cem Sultan, Bayezid II's rival brother.

quote.text: In March 1489, Cem, the captive brother of Bayezid II, the sultan of the Ottoman Empire, came into Innocent's custody. Viewing his brother as a rival, the Sultan paid Pope Innocent not to set him free.

records: Pope Innocent VIII, leader of the Roman Catholic Church since 1484, dies at the age of 59 from catarrh.

Pope Innocent VIII and members of the College of Cardinals meet at the church of Santa Maria del Popolo in Rome with diplomatic envoys sent by the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II. The envoys present the Pope a gift, said to be the Holy Lance, from the Sultan, along with the Sultan's proposal, payment of 120,000 crowns of gold and an annual subsidy of 45,000 ducats in return for the continued imprisonment of Cem Sultan, a half-brother of Bayezid and a rival claimant to the throne.
Pope Innocent VIII (b. 1432)

anchors.heading: La Palma
anchors.prose: Castilian troops began the conquest of La Palma in the Canary Islands. On 3 May, Alonso Fernández de Lugo completed the conquest by capturing the Guanche king Tanausu.

quote.text: The seven main islands, listed from largest to smallest by area, are Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, La Palma, La Gomera, and El Hierro. The only other inhabited island is La Graciosa, which is administratively dependent on Lanzarote.

records: Castilian troops starts the conquest of the island of La Palma in the Canary Islands.
In the Canary Islands, the Spanish conquistador Alonso Fernandez de Lugo finishes the conquest of the island of La Palma by capturing Tanausu, King of the native Guanches.

image.commons_file: File:Alhambra Decree.jpg

anchors.prose: Ferdinand and Isabella signed the Alhambra Decree on 31 March, ordering all unconverted Jews to leave Spain by the end of July. On 2 August, the Tisha B'Av fast day, between 40,000 and 200,000 Jews were expelled. Sultan Bayezid II sent the Ottoman Navy to bring many to Ottoman lands, especially Thessaloniki and İzmir. In November, the Catholic Monarchs issued an ordinance allowing Jews who had left to return if they converted to Catholicism.

quote.text: On 31 March 1492, the Catholic Monarchs of Spain, King Ferdinand II of Aragon and Queen Isabella I of Castile, issued the Alhambra Decree, ordering all unconverted Jews to leave their kingdoms and territories by the end of July that year, unless they converted to Christianity.

records: The Catholic Monarchs of Spain issue an Ordinance legalizing the return of Sephardi Jews who had been expelled in August and the terms for remaining. In both cases, all need a baptism as Christian converts in the Roman Catholic church.
Ferdinand and Isabella sign the Alhambra Decree, expelling all Jews from Spain unless they convert to Roman Catholicism.

The Jews are expelled from Spain on the Tisha B'Av fast day, pursuant to the Alhambra Decree. More than 40,000 and perhaps as many as 200,000 leave. Sultan Bayezid II of the Ottoman Empire, learning of this, dispatches the Ottoman Navy to bring the Jews safely to Ottoman lands, mainly to the cities of Thessaloniki (in modern-day Greece) and İzmir (in modern-day Turkey); others settle in Sarajevo.

overview.prose: Granada fell at the start of the year, ending 780 years of Muslim rule in Al-Andalus. In March, the Catholic Monarchs signed the Alhambra Decree, expelling unconverted Jews; tens of thousands left during the summer. The papal tiara changed hands twice: Innocent VIII died in July, and Rodrigo Borja was elected Alexander VI in August. Christopher Columbus, after securing royal backing in April, sailed from Palos in August and made landfall in the Caribbean in October, believing he had reached the East Indies. Henry VII of England besieged Boulogne in October and concluded the Peace of Étaples in November, accepting a large indemnity. The year's records are thickest around Spanish expansion, papal politics, and the opening of the Atlantic.

The Columbus expedition, having seen no land for 29 days while sailing eastward, and with some of its sailors threatening to mutiny, spots large flocks of birds, confirming that land is ahead. Christopher Columbus orders a change of course to follow the flight direction of the birds.
The day before sighting land for the first time in a month, Columbus quells an attempt at mutiny by sailors who demand that he turn the Niña around to sail back to Spain.

register_entries.text: Believing he has reached the East Indies, Christopher Columbus and his expedition of three ships make landfall in the Caribbean and land on the island of Guanahani, now part of the Bahamas. He names the island "San Salvador". Earlier in the day, sailor Rodrigo de Triana on the Pinta had become the first person to spot land. Because of his belief that he is in the East Indies, Columbus refers to the natives as "indios".

sections.heading: Rulers, wars and states
sections.prose: Granada fell to the Catholic Monarchs on 2 January, ending the Reconquista. Casimir IV Jagiellon died in June; Alexander Jagiellon succeeded as Grand Duke of Lithuania, and John I Albert was crowned King of Poland in September. Elizabeth Woodville, the Yorkist queen dowager, died in June. Pope Innocent VIII died in July; Rodrigo Borja was elected Alexander VI in August. Henry VII of England besieged Boulogne in October, but the Peace of Étaples in November brought a French indemnity and the end of support for Perkin Warbeck. Columbus reached Hispaniola in December and abandoned the Santa María after it ran aground on 25 December; Guacanagaríx allowed 39 men to stay. In West Africa, Sonni Baru became emperor of Songhai. The Russians built Ivangorod Fortress on the Narva River.

sections.heading: Religion and reform
sections.prose: The Titulus Crucis relic was discovered during renovations at Santa Croce in Gerusalemme in Rome. The Alhambra Decree of 31 March ordered the expulsion of unconverted Jews from Spain. In May, Pope Innocent VIII received Ottoman envoys bearing the Holy Lance and an offer of payment to keep Cem Sultan imprisoned. The August conclave in the Sistine Chapel elected Rodrigo Borja as Pope Alexander VI.

sections.heading: Science, scholarship and exploration
sections.prose: Christopher Columbus, after 29 days without sighting land, followed flocks of birds on 7 October and quelled a mutiny on 10 October. Landfall on Guanahani came on 12 October; Columbus named it San Salvador and called the natives indios. He landed in Cuba on 28 October. Marsilio Ficino published his translation and commentary of Plotinus. Martin Behaim constructed the Erdapfel, the oldest surviving globe, which showed no New World.

sections.heading: Art, music and letters
sections.prose: Antonio de Nebrija published the first grammar of Castilian Spanish in Salamanca. The Soncino Bible, a Hebrew printed edition, appeared on 23 January. The expulsion of Jews from Spain began on 2 August; Bayezid II dispatched the Ottoman Navy to evacuate many to Thessaloniki, İzmir, and Sarajevo. In November, an ordinance allowed baptized Jews to return. Ermysted's Grammar School was founded in Skipton. Stiegl brewery was first recorded in Salzburg.

sections.heading: Trade and movement
sections.prose: Columbus met Ferdinand and Isabella at Córdoba in January and secured their support. The Capitulations of Santa Fe were signed in April. A royal decree at Palos in April commanded ships and crews for the voyage. Columbus sailed from Palos on 3 August with three ships, stopping at La Gomera on 6 September before crossing the Atlantic. In Ming China, the grain-for-salt certificate system was monetized.

sections.heading: Earth, weather and disease
sections.prose: The Ensisheim meteorite fell in a wheat field in Alsace on 7 November. The first arboretum was planted at Trsteno near Dubrovnik.

sections.heading: Elsewhere in the year
sections.prose: Anne of Brittany was crowned queen of France in February. Perkin Warbeck was brought to Harfleur by the French fleet. The Alhambra Decree was issued on 31 March. Alexander Plunket became Lord Chancellor of Ireland; Walter Fitzsimon was appointed Lord Deputy. Castilian troops began the conquest of La Palma. Catherine of Navarre won the civil war in Navarre. James Ormonde became Lord Treasurer of Ireland. A possible eruption of Teide was noted in Columbus's log. The Butler–Fitzgerald dispute was resolved in Dublin. The ceiling of the Aljafería Palace in Zaragoza was finished. Diego de San Pedro's novel Cárcel de amor was printed in Seville.
